units.leftText: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
units.rightText: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.

units.leftText: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
units.rightText: He had seven sons and three daughters,

units.leftText: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
units.rightText: and he owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys, and a very large number of servants. Job was the greatest man of all the people of the East.

units.leftText: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
units.rightText: Job’s sons would take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

units.leftText: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.
units.rightText: And when the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children to purify them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. For Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular practice. Satan’s First Attack

units.leftText: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
units.rightText: Now when Job’s three friends— Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite— heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.

units.leftText: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
units.rightText: When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.

units.leftText: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

units.rightText: For now you are of no help; you see terror, and you are afraid.

units.leftText: Did I ever say, ‘Give to me’? or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance’?
units.rightText: Have I ever said, ‘Give me something; offer me a bribe from your wealth;

units.leftText: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’? or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors’?
units.rightText: deliver me from the hand of the enemy; redeem me from the grasp of the ruthless’ ?

units.leftText: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.
units.rightText: Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.

units.leftText: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
units.rightText: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?

units.leftText: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
units.rightText: Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?

units.leftText: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
units.rightText: You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.

units.leftText: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.
units.rightText: But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?

units.leftText: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
units.rightText: Reconsider; do not be unjust. Reconsider, for my righteousness is at stake.

units.leftText: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
units.rightText: Is there iniquity on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern malice?[’’]

units.leftText: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
units.rightText: “Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?

units.leftText: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
units.rightText: Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.

units.leftText: so I am made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
units.rightText: So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed to me.

units.leftText: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
units.rightText: When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.

units.leftText: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
units.rightText: My flesh is clothed with worms and encrusted with dirt; my skin is cracked and festering.

units.leftText: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
units.rightText: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.

units.leftText: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.
units.rightText: Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.

units.leftText: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.
units.rightText: The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.

units.leftText: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol will come up no more.
units.rightText: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
leftNotes: 7:9 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.
units.rightText: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.

units.leftText: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
units.rightText: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

units.leftText: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
units.rightText: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?

units.leftText: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint,’
units.rightText: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,

units.leftText: then you scare me with dreams and terrify me through visions,
units.rightText: then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,

units.leftText: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
units.rightText: so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.

units.leftText: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
units.rightText: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

units.leftText: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
units.rightText: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him,

units.leftText: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
units.rightText: that You attend to him every morning, and test him every moment?

units.leftText: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
units.rightText: Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?

units.leftText: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
units.rightText: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You ?

units.leftText: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.”
units.rightText: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,
units.rightText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

units.leftText: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
units.rightText: “How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.

units.leftText: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
units.rightText: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?

units.leftText: If your children have sinned against him, he has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.
units.rightText: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.

units.leftText: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.
units.rightText: But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy,

units.leftText: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.
units.rightText: if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and restore your righteous estate.

units.leftText: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.
units.rightText: Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.

units.leftText: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.
units.rightText: Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.

units.leftText: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
units.rightText: For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.

units.leftText: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
units.rightText: Will they not teach you and tell you, and speak from their understanding?

units.leftText: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?
units.rightText: Does papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Do reeds flourish without water?

units.leftText: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
units.rightText: While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up more quickly than grass.

units.leftText: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man will perish,
units.rightText: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.

units.leftText: whose confidence will break apart, whose trust is a spider’s web.
units.rightText: His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.

units.leftText: He will lean on his house, but it will not stand. He will cling to it, but it will not endure.
units.rightText: He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.

units.leftText: He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.
units.rightText: He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden.

units.leftText: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.
units.rightText: His roots wrap around the rock heap; he looks for a home among the stones.

units.leftText: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
units.rightText: If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘ I never saw you.’

units.leftText: Behold, this is the joy of his way. Out of the earth, others will spring.
units.rightText: Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust.

units.leftText: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.
units.rightText: Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.

units.leftText: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.
units.rightText: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.

units.leftText: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked will be no more.”
units.rightText: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
units.rightText: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?

units.leftText: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
units.rightText: If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
rightNotes: 9:3 Or If God wished to contend with someone

units.leftText: God is wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against him and prospered?
units.rightText: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?

units.leftText: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
units.rightText: He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.

units.leftText: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
units.rightText: He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.

units.leftText: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
units.rightText: He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.

units.leftText: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
units.rightText: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.

units.leftText: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
units.rightText: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.

units.leftText: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
units.rightText: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.

units.leftText: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
units.rightText: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.

units.leftText: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
units.rightText: If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’

units.leftText: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
units.rightText: God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.

units.leftText: How much less will I answer him, and choose my words to argue with him?
units.rightText: How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?

units.leftText: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
units.rightText: For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.

units.leftText: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
units.rightText: If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.

units.leftText: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
units.rightText: For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.

units.leftText: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
units.rightText: He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.

units.leftText: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
units.rightText: If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him ?

units.leftText: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
units.rightText: Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
rightNotes: 9:20 Or He would declare me guilty

units.leftText: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
units.rightText: Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.

units.leftText: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
units.rightText: It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’

units.leftText: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
units.rightText: When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.

units.leftText: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
units.rightText: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?

units.leftText: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
units.rightText: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.

units.leftText: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
units.rightText: They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.

units.leftText: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up,’
units.rightText: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’

units.leftText: I am afraid of all my sorrows. I know that you will not hold me innocent.
units.rightText: I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.

units.leftText: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
units.rightText: Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?

units.leftText: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
units.rightText: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,

units.leftText: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.
units.rightText: then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.

units.leftText: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
units.rightText: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.

units.leftText: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
units.rightText: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.

units.leftText: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
units.rightText: Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.

units.leftText: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
units.rightText: Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.[’’]

units.leftText: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
units.rightText: “I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint and speak in the bitterness of my soul.

units.leftText: I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.
units.rightText: I will say to God: Do not condemn me! Let me know why You prosecute me.

units.leftText: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?
units.rightText: Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?

units.leftText: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?
units.rightText: Do You have eyes of flesh? Do You see as man sees?

units.leftText: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man’s years,
units.rightText: Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man,

units.leftText: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?
units.rightText: that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin —

units.leftText: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.
units.rightText: though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?

units.leftText: “‘Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.
units.rightText: Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?

units.leftText: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?
units.rightText: Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?

units.leftText: Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
units.rightText: Did You not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?

units.leftText: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
units.rightText: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.

units.leftText: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.
units.rightText: You have granted me life and loving devotion, and Your care has preserved my spirit.
rightNotes: 10:12 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:
units.rightText: Yet You concealed these things in Your heart, and I know that this was in Your mind:

units.leftText: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.
units.rightText: If I sinned, You would take note, and would not acquit me of my iniquity.

units.leftText: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still will not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.
units.rightText: If I am guilty, woe to me! And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of shame and aware of my affliction.

units.leftText: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.
units.rightText: Should I hold my head high, You would hunt me like a lion, and again display Your power against me.

units.leftText: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.
units.rightText: You produce new witnesses against me and multiply Your anger toward me. Hardships assault me in wave after wave.

units.leftText: “‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.
units.rightText: Why then did You bring me from the womb? Oh, that I had died, and no eye had seen me!

units.leftText: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
units.rightText: If only I had never come to be, but had been carried from the womb to the grave.

units.leftText: Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
units.rightText: Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort,

units.leftText: before I go where I will not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
units.rightText: before I go — never to return — to a land of darkness and gloom,

units.leftText: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’”
units.rightText: to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”

units.leftText: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,
units.rightText: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

units.leftText: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
units.rightText: “Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?

units.leftText: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?
units.rightText: Should your babbling put others to silence? Will you scoff without rebuke?

units.leftText: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’
units.rightText: You have said, ‘My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight.’

units.leftText: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
units.rightText: But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,

units.leftText: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
units.rightText: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.

units.leftText: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
units.rightText: Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?

units.leftText: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
units.rightText: They are higher than the heavens— what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol— what can you know?
leftNotes: 11:8 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
units.rightText: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.

units.leftText: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
units.rightText: If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?

units.leftText: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.
units.rightText: Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?

units.leftText: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
units.rightText: But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!

units.leftText: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
units.rightText: As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,

units.leftText: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
units.rightText: if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents,

units.leftText: Surely then you will lift up your face without spot. Yes, you will be steadfast, and will not fear,
units.rightText: then indeed you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm and unafraid.

units.leftText: for you will forget your misery. You will remember it like waters that have passed away.
units.rightText: For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.

units.leftText: Life will be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.
units.rightText: Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.

units.leftText: You will be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you will search, and will take your rest in safety.
units.rightText: You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.

units.leftText: Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. Yes, many will court your favor.
units.rightText: You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.

units.leftText: But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They will have no way to flee. Their hope will be the giving up of the spirit.”
units.rightText: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom will die with you.
units.rightText: “Truly then you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die!

units.leftText: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?
units.rightText: But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?

units.leftText: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.
units.rightText: I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered. The righteous and upright man is a laughingstock.

units.leftText: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
units.rightText: The one at ease scorns misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

units.leftText: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their god in their hands.
units.rightText: The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure — those who carry their god in their hands.
rightNotes: 12:6 Or though God keeps them in His power

units.leftText: “But ask the animals now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
units.rightText: But ask the animals, and they will instruct you; ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you.

units.leftText: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you. The fish of the sea will declare to you.
units.rightText: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea inform you.

units.leftText: Who doesn’t know that in all these, the LORD’s hand has done this,
units.rightText: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?

units.leftText: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
units.rightText: The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.

units.leftText: Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?
units.rightText: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?

units.leftText: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.
units.rightText: Wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life.

units.leftText: “With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.
units.rightText: Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.

units.leftText: Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
units.rightText: What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.

units.leftText: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
units.rightText: If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.

units.leftText: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.
units.rightText: True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.

units.leftText: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
units.rightText: He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.

units.leftText: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.
units.rightText: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.

units.leftText: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
units.rightText: He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows the established.

units.leftText: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.
units.rightText: He deprives the trusted of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.

units.leftText: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.
units.rightText: He pours out contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.

units.leftText: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.
units.rightText: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light.

units.leftText: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.
units.rightText: He makes nations great and destroys them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.

units.leftText: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
units.rightText: He deprives the earth’s leaders of reason and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland.

units.leftText: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.
units.rightText: They grope in the darkness without light; He makes them stagger like drunkards.[’’]

units.leftText: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.
units.rightText: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood.

units.leftText: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.
units.rightText: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.

units.leftText: “Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.
units.rightText: Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.

units.leftText: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.
units.rightText: You, however, smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.

units.leftText: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
units.rightText: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!

units.leftText: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.
units.rightText: Hear now my argument, and listen to the plea of my lips.

units.leftText: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?
units.rightText: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?

units.leftText: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?
units.rightText: Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?

units.leftText: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?
units.rightText: Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him as you would deceive a man?

units.leftText: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.
units.rightText: Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.

units.leftText: Won’t his majesty make you afraid and his dread fall on you?
units.rightText: Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?

units.leftText: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes. Your defenses are defenses of clay.
units.rightText: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.

units.leftText: “Be silent! Leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.
units.rightText: Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may.

units.leftText: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
units.rightText: Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?
rightNotes: 13:14 Literally Why do I take my flesh in my teeth

units.leftText: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.
units.rightText: Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
rightNotes: 13:15 Or I have no other hope

units.leftText: This also will be my salvation, that a godless man will not come before him.
units.rightText: Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.

units.leftText: Listen carefully to my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.
units.rightText: Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears.

units.leftText: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.
units.rightText: See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.

units.leftText: Who is he who will contend with me? For then I would hold my peace and give up the spirit.
units.rightText: Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.

units.leftText: “Only don’t do two things to me, then I will not hide myself from your face:
units.rightText: Only grant these two things to me, so that I need not hide from You:

units.leftText: withdraw your hand far from me, and don’t let your terror make me afraid.
units.rightText: Withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror frighten me.

units.leftText: Then call, and I will answer, or let me speak, and you answer me.
units.rightText: Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.

units.leftText: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.
units.rightText: How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.

units.leftText: Why do you hide your face, and consider me your enemy?
units.rightText: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?

units.leftText: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
units.rightText: Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?

units.leftText: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
units.rightText: For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.

units.leftText: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,
units.rightText: You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.

units.leftText: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
units.rightText: So man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment.[’’]

units.leftText: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
units.rightText: “Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.

units.leftText: He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.
units.rightText: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.

units.leftText: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?
units.rightText: Do You open Your eyes to one like this? Will You bring him into judgment before You?

units.leftText: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.
units.rightText: Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!

units.leftText: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can’t pass.
units.rightText: Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,

units.leftText: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he accomplishes, as a hireling, his day.
units.rightText: look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.

units.leftText: “For there is hope for a tree if it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.
units.rightText: For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoots will not fail.

units.leftText: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,
units.rightText: If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,

units.leftText: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.
units.rightText: at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.

units.leftText: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?
units.rightText: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?

units.leftText: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,
units.rightText: As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry,

units.leftText: so man lies down and doesn’t rise. Until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.
units.rightText: so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.

units.leftText: “Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would keep me secret until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time and remember me!
units.rightText: If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!
leftNotes: 14:13 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: If a man dies, will he live again? I would wait all the days of my warfare, until my release should come.
units.rightText: When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.
rightNotes: 14:14 Or my change or my relief

units.leftText: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire for the work of your hands.
units.rightText: You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.

units.leftText: But now you count my steps. Don’t you watch over my sin?
units.rightText: For then You would count my steps, but would not keep track of my sin.

units.leftText: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.
units.rightText: My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.

units.leftText: “But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place.
units.rightText: But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place,

units.leftText: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.
units.rightText: as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil, so You destroy a man’s hope.

units.leftText: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.
units.rightText: You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.

units.leftText: His sons come to honor, and he doesn’t know it. They are brought low, but he doesn’t perceive it of them.
units.rightText: If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.

units.leftText: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns.”
units.rightText: He feels only the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself.”

units.leftText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,
units.rightText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

units.leftText: “Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?
units.rightText: “Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?

units.leftText: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?
units.rightText: Should he argue with useless words or speeches that serve no purpose?

units.leftText: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.
units.rightText: But you even undermine the fear of God and hinder meditation before Him.

units.leftText: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
units.rightText: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.

units.leftText: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.
units.rightText: Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.

units.leftText: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought out before the hills?
units.rightText: Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?

units.leftText: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?
units.rightText: Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?

units.leftText: What do you know that we don’t know? What do you understand which is not in us?
units.rightText: What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is not clear to us?

units.leftText: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much older than your father.
units.rightText: Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side — men much older than your father.

units.leftText: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?
units.rightText: Are the consolations of God not enough for you, even words spoken gently to you?

units.leftText: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
units.rightText: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,

units.leftText: that you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?
units.rightText: so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?

units.leftText: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
units.rightText: What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?

units.leftText: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;
units.rightText: If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes,

units.leftText: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!
units.rightText: how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?

units.leftText: “I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare
units.rightText: Listen to me and I will inform you. I will describe what I have seen,

units.leftText: (which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;
units.rightText: what was declared by wise men and was not concealed from their fathers,

units.leftText: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):
units.rightText: to whom alone the land was given when no foreigner passed among them.

units.leftText: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
units.rightText: A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.

units.leftText: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer will come on him.
units.rightText: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.

units.leftText: He doesn’t believe that he will return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.
units.rightText: He despairs of his return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.

units.leftText: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
units.rightText: He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.

units.leftText: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
units.rightText: Distress and anguish terrify him, overwhelming him like a king poised to attack.

units.leftText: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty,
units.rightText: For he has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty,

units.leftText: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers,
units.rightText: rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.

units.leftText: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.
units.rightText: Though his face is covered with fat and his waistline bulges with flesh,

units.leftText: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.
units.rightText: he will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.

units.leftText: He will not be rich, neither will his substance continue, neither will their possessions be extended on the earth.
units.rightText: He will no longer be rich; his wealth will not endure. His possessions will not overspread the land.

units.leftText: He will not depart out of darkness. The flame will dry up his branches. He will go away by the breath of God’s mouth.
units.rightText: He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.

units.leftText: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.
units.rightText: Let him not deceive himself with trust in emptiness, for emptiness will be his reward.

units.leftText: It will be accomplished before his time. His branch will not be green.
units.rightText: It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not flourish.

units.leftText: He will shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and will cast off his flower as the olive tree.
units.rightText: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.

units.leftText: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
units.rightText: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.

units.leftText: They conceive mischief and produce iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit.”
units.rightText: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb is pregnant with deceit.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!
units.rightText: “I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.

units.leftText: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
units.rightText: Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?

units.leftText: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,
units.rightText: I could also speak like you if you were in my place; I could heap up words against you and shake my head at you.

units.leftText: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.
units.rightText: But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.

units.leftText: “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?
units.rightText: Even if I speak, my pain is not relieved, and if I hold back, how will it go away?

units.leftText: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made all my company desolate.
units.rightText: Surely He has now exhausted me; You have devastated all my family.

units.leftText: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.
units.rightText: You have bound me, and it has become a witness; my frailty rises up and testifies against me.

units.leftText: He has torn me in his wrath and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.
units.rightText: His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me. My adversary pierces me with His eyes.

units.leftText: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.
units.rightText: They open their mouths against me and strike my cheeks with contempt; they join together against me.

units.leftText: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
units.rightText: God has delivered me to unjust men; He has thrown me to the clutches of the wicked.

units.leftText: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.
units.rightText: I was at ease, but He shattered me; He seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has set me up as His target;

units.leftText: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my bile on the ground.
units.rightText: His archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without mercy and spills my gall on the ground.

units.leftText: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs at me like a giant.
units.rightText: He breaks me with wound upon wound; He rushes me like a mighty warrior.

units.leftText: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.
units.rightText: I have sewn sackcloth over my skin; I have buried my horn in the dust.

units.leftText: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids,
units.rightText: My face is red with weeping, and deep shadows ring my eyes;

units.leftText: although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
units.rightText: yet my hands are free of violence and my prayer is pure.

units.leftText: “Earth, don’t cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.
units.rightText: O earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry for help never be laid to rest.

units.leftText: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.
units.rightText: Even now my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.

units.leftText: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,
units.rightText: My friends are my scoffers as my eyes pour out tears to God.

units.leftText: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!
units.rightText: Oh, that a man might plead with God as he pleads with his neighbor!

units.leftText: For when a few years have come, I will go the way of no return.
units.rightText: For when only a few years are past I will go the way of no return.[’’]

units.leftText: “My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct and the grave is ready for me.
units.rightText: “My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; the grave awaits me.

units.leftText: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.
units.rightText: Surely mockers surround me, and my eyes must gaze at their rebellion.

units.leftText: “Now give a pledge. Be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?
units.rightText: Give me, I pray, the pledge You demand. Who else will be my guarantor?

units.leftText: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, therefore you will not exalt them.
units.rightText: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.

units.leftText: He who denounces his friends for plunder, even the eyes of his children will fail.
units.rightText: If a man denounces his friends for a price, the eyes of his children will fail.

units.leftText: “But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.
units.rightText: He has made me a byword among the people, a man in whose face they spit.

units.leftText: My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.
units.rightText: My eyes have grown dim with grief, and my whole body is but a shadow.

units.leftText: Upright men will be astonished at this. The innocent will stir himself up against the godless.
units.rightText: The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred against the godless.

units.leftText: Yet the righteous will hold to his way. He who has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.
units.rightText: Yet a righteous one holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.

units.leftText: But as for you all, come back. I will not find a wise man among you.
units.rightText: But come back and try again, all of you. For I will not find a wise man among you.

units.leftText: My days are past. My plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
units.rightText: My days have passed; my plans are broken off — even the desires of my heart.

units.leftText: They change the night into day, saying ‘The light is near’ in the presence of darkness.
units.rightText: They have turned night into day, making light seem near in the face of darkness.

units.leftText: If I look for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,
units.rightText: If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
leftNotes: 17:13 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: if I have said to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ and ‘My sister,’
units.rightText: and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’

units.leftText: where then is my hope? As for my hope, who will see it?
units.rightText: where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?

units.leftText: Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol, or descend together into the dust?”
units.rightText: Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”
leftNotes: 17:16 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,
units.rightText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

units.leftText: “How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.
units.rightText: “How long until you end these speeches? Show some sense, and then we can talk.

units.leftText: Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in your sight?
units.rightText: Why are we regarded as cattle, as stupid in your sight?

units.leftText: You who tear yourself in your anger, will the earth be forsaken for you? Or will the rock be removed out of its place?
units.rightText: You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account, or the rocks be moved from their place?

units.leftText: “Yes, the light of the wicked will be put out. The spark of his fire won’t shine.
units.rightText: Indeed, the lamp of the wicked is extinguished; the flame of his fire does not glow.

units.leftText: The light will be dark in his tent. His lamp above him will be put out.
units.rightText: The light in his tent grows dark, and the lamp beside him goes out.

units.leftText: The steps of his strength will be shortened. His own counsel will cast him down.
units.rightText: His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up.

units.leftText: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.
units.rightText: For his own feet lead him into a net, and he wanders into its mesh.

units.leftText: A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.
units.rightText: A trap seizes his heel; a snare grips him.

units.leftText: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him on the path.
units.rightText: A noose is hidden in the ground, and a trap lies in his path.

units.leftText: Terrors will make him afraid on every side, and will chase him at his heels.
units.rightText: Terrors frighten him on every side and harass his every step.

units.leftText: His strength will be famished. Calamity will be ready at his side.
units.rightText: His strength is depleted, and calamity is ready at his side.

units.leftText: The members of his body will be devoured. The firstborn of death will devour his members.
units.rightText: It devours patches of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.

units.leftText: He will be rooted out of the security of his tent. He will be brought to the king of terrors.
units.rightText: He is torn from the shelter of his tent and is marched off to the king of terrors.

units.leftText: There will dwell in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur will be scattered on his habitation.
units.rightText: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur rains down on his dwelling.

units.leftText: His roots will be dried up beneath. His branch will be cut off above.
units.rightText: The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.

units.leftText: His memory will perish from the earth. He will have no name in the street.
units.rightText: The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.

units.leftText: He will be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
units.rightText: He is driven from light into darkness and is chased from the inhabited world.

units.leftText: He will have neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he lived.
units.rightText: He has no offspring or posterity among his people, no survivor where he once lived.

units.leftText: Those who come after will be astonished at his day, as those who went before were frightened.
units.rightText: Those in the west are appalled at his fate, while those in the east tremble in horror.

units.leftText: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who doesn’t know God.”
units.rightText: Surely such is the dwelling of the wicked and the place of one who does not know God.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?
units.rightText: “How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?

units.leftText: You have reproached me ten times. You aren’t ashamed that you attack me.
units.rightText: Ten times now you have reproached me; you shamelessly mistreat me.

units.leftText: If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.
units.rightText: Even if I have truly gone astray, my error concerns me alone.

units.leftText: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach,
units.rightText: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my disgrace against me,

units.leftText: know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.
units.rightText: then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.

units.leftText: “Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.
units.rightText: Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.

units.leftText: He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass, and has set darkness in my paths.
units.rightText: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; He has veiled my paths with darkness.

units.leftText: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
units.rightText: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.

units.leftText: He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. He has plucked my hope up like a tree.
units.rightText: He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.

units.leftText: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.
units.rightText: His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.

units.leftText: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.
units.rightText: His troops advance together; they construct a ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

units.leftText: “He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.
units.rightText: He has removed my brothers from me; my acquaintances have abandoned me.

units.leftText: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
units.rightText: My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.

units.leftText: Those who dwell in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I am an alien in their sight.
units.rightText: My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.

units.leftText: I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.
units.rightText: I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.

units.leftText: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.
units.rightText: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own family.

units.leftText: Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.
units.rightText: Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.

units.leftText: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.
units.rightText: All my best friends despise me, and those I love have turned against me.

units.leftText: My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
units.rightText: My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

units.leftText: “Have pity on me. Have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me.
units.rightText: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.

units.leftText: Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
units.rightText: Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?

units.leftText: “Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!
units.rightText: I wish that my words were recorded and inscribed in a book,

units.leftText: That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!
units.rightText: by an iron stylus on lead, or chiseled in stone forever.

units.leftText: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
units.rightText: But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.

units.leftText: After my skin is destroyed, then I will see God in my flesh,
units.rightText: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.

units.leftText: whom I, even I, will see on my side. My eyes will see, and not as a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me.
units.rightText: I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. How my heart yearns within me!

units.leftText: If you say, ‘How we will persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is found in me,
units.rightText: If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him, ’
rightNotes: 19:28 Many Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, and Vulgate; most Hebrew manuscripts with me

units.leftText: be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment.”
units.rightText: then you should fear the sword yourselves, because wrath brings punishment by the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.”

units.leftText: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered,
units.rightText: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

units.leftText: “Therefore my thoughts answer me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
units.rightText: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.

units.leftText: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.
units.rightText: I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply.

units.leftText: Don’t you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,
units.rightText: Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,

units.leftText: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?
units.rightText: the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?

units.leftText: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,
units.rightText: Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds,

units.leftText: yet he will perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’
units.rightText: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’

units.leftText: He will fly away as a dream, and will not be found. Yes, he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
units.rightText: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.

units.leftText: The eye which saw him will see him no more, neither will his place see him any more.
units.rightText: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.

units.leftText: His children will seek the favor of the poor. His hands will give back his wealth.
units.rightText: His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.

units.leftText: His bones are full of his youth, but youth will lie down with him in the dust.
units.rightText: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.

units.leftText: “Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,
units.rightText: Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,

units.leftText: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth,
units.rightText: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,

units.leftText: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.
units.rightText: yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.

units.leftText: He has swallowed down riches, and he will vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.
units.rightText: He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach.

units.leftText: He will suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue will kill him.
units.rightText: He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.

units.leftText: He will not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.
units.rightText: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.

units.leftText: He will restore that for which he labored, and will not swallow it down. He will not rejoice according to the substance that he has gotten.
units.rightText: He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.

units.leftText: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he will not build it up.
units.rightText: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.

units.leftText: “Because he knew no quietness within him, he will not save anything of that in which he delights.
units.rightText: Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.

units.leftText: There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, therefore his prosperity will not endure.
units.rightText: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.

units.leftText: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress will overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery will come on him.
units.rightText: In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.

units.leftText: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.
units.rightText: When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.

units.leftText: He will flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow will strike him through.
units.rightText: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.

units.leftText: He draws it out, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.
units.rightText: It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.

units.leftText: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire will devour him. It will consume that which is left in his tent.
units.rightText: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

units.leftText: The heavens will reveal his iniquity. The earth will rise up against him.
units.rightText: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.

units.leftText: The increase of his house will depart. They will rush away in the day of his wrath.
units.rightText: The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.

units.leftText: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God.”
units.rightText: This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.
units.rightText: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.

units.leftText: Allow me, and I also will speak. After I have spoken, mock on.
units.rightText: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.

units.leftText: As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn’t I be impatient?
units.rightText: Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?

units.leftText: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth.
units.rightText: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.

units.leftText: When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.
units.rightText: When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.

units.leftText: “Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?
units.rightText: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?

units.leftText: Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.
units.rightText: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.

units.leftText: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
units.rightText: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.

units.leftText: Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don’t miscarry.
units.rightText: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.

units.leftText: They send out their little ones like a flock. Their children dance.
units.rightText: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,

units.leftText: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
units.rightText: singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.

units.leftText: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol.
units.rightText: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
leftNotes: 21:13 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: They tell God, ‘Depart from us, for we don’t want to know about your ways.
units.rightText: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.

units.leftText: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?’
units.rightText: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’

units.leftText: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
units.rightText: Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

units.leftText: “How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?
units.rightText: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?

units.leftText: How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?
units.rightText: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?

units.leftText: You say, ‘God lays up his iniquity for his children.’ Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it.
units.rightText: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.

units.leftText: Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
units.rightText: Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.

units.leftText: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
units.rightText: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?

units.leftText: “Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high?
units.rightText: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?

units.leftText: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
units.rightText: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.

units.leftText: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.
units.rightText: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.
rightNotes: 21:24 Literally His pails are full of milk

units.leftText: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.
units.rightText: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.

units.leftText: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.
units.rightText: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.

units.leftText: “Behold, I know your thoughts, the plans with which you would wrong me.
units.rightText: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

units.leftText: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’
units.rightText: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’

units.leftText: Haven’t you asked wayfaring men? Don’t you know their evidences,
units.rightText: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?

units.leftText: that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, that they are led out to the day of wrath?
units.rightText: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.

units.leftText: Who will declare his way to his face? Who will repay him what he has done?
units.rightText: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?

units.leftText: Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men will keep watch over the tomb.
units.rightText: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.

units.leftText: The clods of the valley will be sweet to him. All men will draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.
units.rightText: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.

units.leftText: So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?”
units.rightText: So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”

units.leftText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,
units.rightText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

units.leftText: “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.
units.rightText: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?

units.leftText: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him that you make your ways perfect?
