units.rightText: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?

units.leftText: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?
units.rightText: Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?

units.leftText: Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.
units.rightText: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?

units.leftText: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
units.rightText: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.

units.leftText: You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
units.rightText: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,

units.leftText: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.
units.rightText: while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.

units.leftText: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
units.rightText: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.

units.leftText: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,
units.rightText: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;

units.leftText: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.
units.rightText: it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.

units.leftText: “Isn’t God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!
units.rightText: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!

units.leftText: You say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
units.rightText: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?

units.leftText: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn’t see. He walks on the vault of the sky.’
units.rightText: Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven. ’
rightNotes: 22:14 Or heaven’s horizon or the circle of the sky

units.leftText: Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,
units.rightText: Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod?

units.leftText: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,
units.rightText: They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.

units.leftText: who said to God, ‘Depart from us!’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do for us?’
units.rightText: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’

units.leftText: Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
units.rightText: But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

units.leftText: The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule them,
units.rightText: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:

units.leftText: saying, ‘Surely those who rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed their remnant.’
units.rightText: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’

units.leftText: “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace. By it, good will come to you.
units.rightText: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.

units.leftText: Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
units.rightText: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.

units.leftText: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents.
units.rightText: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents

units.leftText: Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.
units.rightText: and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,

units.leftText: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.
units.rightText: then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.

units.leftText: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face to God.
units.rightText: Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.

units.leftText: You will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You will pay your vows.
units.rightText: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.

units.leftText: You will also decree a thing, and it will be established to you. Light will shine on your ways.
units.rightText: Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.

units.leftText: When they cast down, you will say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.
units.rightText: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.

units.leftText: He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”
units.rightText: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
units.rightText: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.

units.leftText: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!
units.rightText: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.

units.leftText: I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
units.rightText: I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.

units.leftText: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me.
units.rightText: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.

units.leftText: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.
units.rightText: Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.

units.leftText: There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge.
units.rightText: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.

units.leftText: “If I go east, he is not there. If I go west, I can’t find him.
units.rightText: If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.

units.leftText: He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him.
units.rightText: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.

units.leftText: But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I will come out like gold.
units.rightText: Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.

units.leftText: My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned away.
units.rightText: My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.

units.leftText: I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
units.rightText: I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.

units.leftText: But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.
units.rightText: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.

units.leftText: For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.
units.rightText: For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.

units.leftText: Therefore I am terrified at his presence. When I consider, I am afraid of him.
units.rightText: Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.

units.leftText: For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.
units.rightText: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.

units.leftText: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.
units.rightText: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.[’’]

units.leftText: “Why aren’t times laid up by the Almighty? Why don’t those who know him see his days?
units.rightText: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?

units.leftText: There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.
units.rightText: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.

units.leftText: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
units.rightText: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.

units.leftText: They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
units.rightText: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

units.leftText: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go out to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children.
units.rightText: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.

units.leftText: They cut their food in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.
units.rightText: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.

units.leftText: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
units.rightText: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.

units.leftText: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.
units.rightText: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.

units.leftText: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,
units.rightText: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.

units.leftText: so that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.
units.rightText: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

units.leftText: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.
units.rightText: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.

units.leftText: From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn’t regard the folly.
units.rightText: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.

units.leftText: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths.
units.rightText: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.

units.leftText: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.
units.rightText: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.

units.leftText: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me.’ He disguises his face.
units.rightText: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.

units.leftText: In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light.
units.rightText: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.

units.leftText: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness.
units.rightText: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!

units.leftText: “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed on the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.
units.rightText: They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.

units.leftText: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol those who have sinned.
units.rightText: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
leftNotes: 24:19 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: The womb will forget him. The worm will feed sweetly on him. He will be no more remembered. Unrighteousness will be broken as a tree.
units.rightText: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.

units.leftText: He devours the barren who don’t bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.
units.rightText: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.

units.leftText: Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.
units.rightText: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.

units.leftText: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways.
units.rightText: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.

units.leftText: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
units.rightText: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

units.leftText: If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”
units.rightText: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,
units.rightText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

units.leftText: “Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.
units.rightText: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.

units.leftText: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?
units.rightText: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?

units.leftText: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?
units.rightText: How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

units.leftText: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight;
units.rightText: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,

units.leftText: How much less man, who is a worm, and the son of man, who is a worm!”
units.rightText: how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”

units.leftText: Then Job answered,
units.rightText: Then Job answered:

units.leftText: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!
units.rightText: “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!

units.leftText: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!
units.rightText: How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!

units.leftText: To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?
units.rightText: To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?

units.leftText: “The departed spirits tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.
units.rightText: The dead tremble — those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.

units.leftText: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
units.rightText: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
leftNotes: 26:6 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.
units.rightText: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing.

units.leftText: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.
units.rightText: He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight.

units.leftText: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.
units.rightText: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading over it His cloud.

units.leftText: He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.
units.rightText: He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.

units.leftText: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
units.rightText: The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke.

units.leftText: He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.
units.rightText: By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.

units.leftText: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.
units.rightText: By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
rightNotes: 26:13 Hebrew nachash; translated in most cases as snake

units.leftText: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”
units.rightText: Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?”

units.leftText: Job again took up his parable, and said,
units.rightText: Job continued his discourse:

units.leftText: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter
units.rightText: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice — the Almighty, who has embittered my soul —

units.leftText: (for the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);
units.rightText: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,

units.leftText: surely my lips will not speak unrighteousness, neither will my tongue utter deceit.
units.rightText: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.

units.leftText: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me.
units.rightText: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.

units.leftText: I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart will not reproach me so long as I live.
units.rightText: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me. The Wicked Man’s Portion

units.leftText: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.
units.rightText: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.

units.leftText: For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
units.rightText: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

units.leftText: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?
units.rightText: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?

units.leftText: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?
units.rightText: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?

units.leftText: I will teach you about the hand of God. I will not conceal that which is with the Almighty.
units.rightText: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.

units.leftText: Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?
units.rightText: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?

units.leftText: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty.
units.rightText: This is the wicked man’s portion from God — the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.

units.leftText: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring will not be satisfied with bread.
units.rightText: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.

units.leftText: Those who remain of him will be buried in death. His widows will make no lamentation.
units.rightText: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.

units.leftText: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
units.rightText: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,

units.leftText: he may prepare it, but the just will put it on, and the innocent will divide the silver.
units.rightText: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.

units.leftText: He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.
units.rightText: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.

units.leftText: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not.
units.rightText: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.

units.leftText: Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.
units.rightText: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.

units.leftText: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.
units.rightText: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.

units.leftText: For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.
units.rightText: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.

units.leftText: Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place.
units.rightText: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.[’’]

units.leftText: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.
units.rightText: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.

units.leftText: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.
units.rightText: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.

units.leftText: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.
units.rightText: Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness.

units.leftText: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.
units.rightText: Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man. Far from men he dangles and sways.

units.leftText: As for the earth, out of it comes bread. Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.
units.rightText: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.

units.leftText: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
units.rightText: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.

units.leftText: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.
units.rightText: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.

units.leftText: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.
units.rightText: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.

units.leftText: He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.
units.rightText: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.

units.leftText: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.
units.rightText: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.

units.leftText: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light.
units.rightText: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.
rightNotes: 28:11 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate He searches

units.leftText: “But where will wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?
units.rightText: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?

units.leftText: Man doesn’t know its price, and it isn’t found in the land of the living.
units.rightText: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.

units.leftText: The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’
units.rightText: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’

units.leftText: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price.
units.rightText: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.

units.leftText: It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
units.rightText: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.

units.leftText: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither will it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
units.rightText: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.

units.leftText: No mention will be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
units.rightText: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.

units.leftText: The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it. It won’t be valued with pure gold.
units.rightText: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
rightNotes: 28:19 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
units.rightText: From where, then, does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?

units.leftText: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.
units.rightText: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.

units.leftText: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
units.rightText: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’

units.leftText: “God understands its way, and he knows its place.
units.rightText: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.

units.leftText: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.
units.rightText: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.

units.leftText: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.
units.rightText: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,

units.leftText: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder,
units.rightText: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,

units.leftText: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.
units.rightText: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.

units.leftText: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”
units.rightText: And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”

units.leftText: Job again took up his parable, and said,
units.rightText: And Job continued his discourse:

units.leftText: “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;
units.rightText: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,

units.leftText: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,
units.rightText: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,

units.leftText: as I was in my prime, when the friendship of God was in my tent,
units.rightText: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
rightNotes: 29:4 Hebrew in the time of my harvest

units.leftText: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me,
units.rightText: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,

units.leftText: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,
units.rightText: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!

units.leftText: when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.
units.rightText: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,

units.leftText: The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.
units.rightText: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.

units.leftText: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.
units.rightText: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.

units.leftText: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
units.rightText: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.

units.leftText: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me, and when the eye saw me, it commended me,
units.rightText: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,

units.leftText: because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had no one to help him,
units.rightText: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.

units.leftText: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
units.rightText: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.

units.leftText: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
units.rightText: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.

units.leftText: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.
units.rightText: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.

units.leftText: I was a father to the needy. I researched the cause of him whom I didn’t know.
units.rightText: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.

units.leftText: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and plucked the prey out of his teeth.
units.rightText: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.

units.leftText: Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.
units.rightText: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.

units.leftText: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.
units.rightText: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.

units.leftText: My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’
units.rightText: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’

units.leftText: “Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.
units.rightText: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.

units.leftText: After my words they didn’t speak again. My speech fell on them.
units.rightText: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.

units.leftText: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain.
units.rightText: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.

units.leftText: I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn’t reject the light of my face.
units.rightText: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.

units.leftText: I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.
units.rightText: I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops, as a comforter of the mourners.[’’]

units.leftText: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I considered unworthy to put with my sheep dogs.
units.rightText: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs.

units.leftText: Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?
units.rightText: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?

units.leftText: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.
units.rightText: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.

units.leftText: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom tree are their food.
units.rightText: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.

units.leftText: They are driven out from among men. They cry after them as after a thief,
units.rightText: They were banished from among men, shouted at like thieves,

units.leftText: so that they live in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.
units.rightText: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

units.leftText: They bray among the bushes. They are gathered together under the nettles.
units.rightText: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.

units.leftText: They are children of fools, yes, children of wicked men. They were flogged out of the land.
units.rightText: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.

units.leftText: “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.
units.rightText: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.

units.leftText: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.
units.rightText: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

units.leftText: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me.
units.rightText: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.

units.leftText: On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet. They cast their ways of destruction up against me.
units.rightText: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.

units.leftText: They mar my path. They promote my destruction without anyone’s help.
units.rightText: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.
rightNotes: 30:13 Or with no one to assist them

units.leftText: As through a wide breach they come. They roll themselves in amid the ruin.
units.rightText: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in. Job’s Prosperity Becomes Calamity

units.leftText: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.
units.rightText: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.

units.leftText: “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold of me.
units.rightText: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.

units.leftText: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
units.rightText: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.

units.leftText: My garment is disfigured by great force. It binds me about as the collar of my tunic.
units.rightText: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.
rightNotes: 30:18 LXX; Hebrew He becomes like a garment to me or my garment is disfigured

units.leftText: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.
units.rightText: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.

units.leftText: I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.
units.rightText: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.

units.leftText: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me.
units.rightText: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.

units.leftText: You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
units.rightText: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.

units.leftText: For I know that you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all living.
units.rightText: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.

units.leftText: “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?
units.rightText: Yet no one stretches out his hand against a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.

units.leftText: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?
units.rightText: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?

units.leftText: When I looked for good, then evil came. When I waited for light, darkness came.
units.rightText: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.

units.leftText: My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.
units.rightText: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.

units.leftText: I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.
units.rightText: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

units.leftText: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.
units.rightText: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
rightNotes: 30:29 Literally of daughters of an ostrich or of daughters of an owl

units.leftText: My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.
units.rightText: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.

units.leftText: Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.
units.rightText: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.[’’]

units.leftText: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
units.rightText: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?

units.leftText: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
units.rightText: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?

units.leftText: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?
units.rightText: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?

units.leftText: Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?
units.rightText: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?

units.leftText: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit
units.rightText: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,

units.leftText: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
units.rightText: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.

units.leftText: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
units.rightText: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,

units.leftText: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
units.rightText: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.

units.leftText: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
units.rightText: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,

units.leftText: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
units.rightText: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.

units.leftText: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges,
units.rightText: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.

units.leftText: for it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
units.rightText: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.

units.leftText: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me,
units.rightText: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,

units.leftText: what then will I do when God rises up? When he visits, what will I answer him?
units.rightText: what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?

units.leftText: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?
units.rightText: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?

units.leftText: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
units.rightText: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,

units.leftText: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
units.rightText: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless —

units.leftText: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, I have guided her from my mother’s womb);
units.rightText: though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow —

units.leftText: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
units.rightText: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,

units.leftText: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
units.rightText: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.

units.leftText: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
units.rightText: Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?

units.leftText: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?
units.rightText: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?

units.leftText: “Remember that you magnify his work, about which men have sung.
units.rightText: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.

units.leftText: All men have looked on it. Man sees it afar off.
units.rightText: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.

units.leftText: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.
units.rightText: Indeed, God is great — beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.

units.leftText: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,
units.rightText: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,

units.leftText: which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
units.rightText: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.

units.leftText: Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds and the thunderings of his pavilion?
units.rightText: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?

units.leftText: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.
units.rightText: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.

units.leftText: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.
units.rightText: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.

units.leftText: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.
units.rightText: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.

units.leftText: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also, concerning the storm that comes up.
units.rightText: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.[’’]

units.leftText: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
units.rightText: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.

units.leftText: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
units.rightText: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.

units.leftText: He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.
units.rightText: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.

units.leftText: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.
units.rightText: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.

units.leftText: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
units.rightText: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’

units.leftText: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
units.rightText: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.

units.leftText: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.
units.rightText: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.

units.leftText: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
units.rightText: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.

units.leftText: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
units.rightText: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.

units.leftText: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
units.rightText: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.

units.leftText: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,
units.rightText: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.

units.leftText: whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.
units.rightText: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.

units.leftText: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
units.rightText: Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.

units.leftText: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
units.rightText: Do you know how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash?

units.leftText: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
units.rightText: Do you understand how the clouds float, those wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge?

units.leftText: You whose clothing is warm when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?
units.rightText: You whose clothes get hot when the land lies hushed under the south wind,

units.leftText: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?
units.rightText: can you, like Him, spread out the skies, as strong as a mirror of bronze?

units.leftText: Teach us what we will tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.
units.rightText: Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.

units.leftText: Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
units.rightText: Should He be told that I want to speak? Would a man ask to be swallowed up ?
rightNotes: 37:20 Or speak without being swallowed up

units.leftText: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.
units.rightText: Now no one can gaze at the sun when it is bright in the skies after the wind has swept them clean.

units.leftText: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
units.rightText: Out of the north He comes in golden splendor; awesome majesty surrounds Him.

units.leftText: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.
units.rightText: The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power! In His justice and great righteousness He does not oppress.

units.leftText: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”
units.rightText: Therefore, men fear Him, for He is not partial to the wise in heart.”

units.leftText: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind,
units.rightText: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

units.leftText: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
units.rightText: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?

units.leftText: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!
units.rightText: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.

units.leftText: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
units.rightText: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.

units.leftText: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?
units.rightText: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?

units.leftText: What were its foundations fastened on? Or who laid its cornerstone,
units.rightText: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone,
rightNotes: 38:6 Or who set its core in place

units.leftText: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
units.rightText: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

units.leftText: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
units.rightText: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,

units.leftText: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
units.rightText: when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket,

units.leftText: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
units.rightText: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,

units.leftText: and said, ‘You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here’?
units.rightText: and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?

units.leftText: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place,
units.rightText: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,

units.leftText: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?
units.rightText: that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?

units.leftText: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
units.rightText: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.

units.leftText: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
units.rightText: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.

units.leftText: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
units.rightText: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?

units.leftText: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
units.rightText: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?

units.leftText: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
units.rightText: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.

units.leftText: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,
units.rightText: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides,

units.leftText: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?
units.rightText: so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?

units.leftText: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
units.rightText: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!

units.leftText: Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
units.rightText: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail,

units.leftText: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
units.rightText: which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?

units.leftText: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?
units.rightText: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?

units.leftText: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm,
units.rightText: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt,

units.leftText: to cause it to rain on a land where there is no man, on the wilderness, in which there is no man,
units.rightText: to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives,

units.leftText: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?
units.rightText: to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?

units.leftText: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
units.rightText: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?

units.leftText: Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?
units.rightText: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven,

units.leftText: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
units.rightText: when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?

units.leftText: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
units.rightText: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?

units.leftText: Can you lead the constellations out in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?
units.rightText: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
rightNotes: 38:32 Or bring forth Mazzaroth in its season

units.leftText: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?
units.rightText: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?

units.leftText: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover you?
units.rightText: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?

units.leftText: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
units.rightText: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?

units.leftText: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?
units.rightText: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
rightNotes: 38:36 Or Who has given the ibis wisdom, that is, wisdom about the flooding of the Nile

units.leftText: Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the containers of the sky,
units.rightText: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens

units.leftText: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?
units.rightText: when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?

units.leftText: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
units.rightText: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions

units.leftText: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
units.rightText: when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?

units.leftText: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?
units.rightText: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?[’’]

units.leftText: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
units.rightText: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?

units.leftText: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
units.rightText: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?

units.leftText: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.
units.rightText: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.

units.leftText: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
units.rightText: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.

units.leftText: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
units.rightText: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?

units.leftText: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
units.rightText: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.

units.leftText: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
units.rightText: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.

units.leftText: The range of the mountains is his pasture. He searches after every green thing.
units.rightText: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.

units.leftText: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
units.rightText: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?

units.leftText: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
units.rightText: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?

units.leftText: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
units.rightText: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?

units.leftText: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
units.rightText: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?

units.leftText: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
units.rightText: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
rightNotes: 39:13 Pinions are the outer parts of a bird’s wings, including the flight feathers.

units.leftText: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
units.rightText: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.

units.leftText: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
units.rightText: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.

units.leftText: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
units.rightText: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.

units.leftText: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
units.rightText: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.

units.leftText: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
units.rightText: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.

units.leftText: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
units.rightText: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?

units.leftText: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
units.rightText: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?

units.leftText: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
units.rightText: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.

units.leftText: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
units.rightText: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.

units.leftText: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
units.rightText: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.

units.leftText: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
units.rightText: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.

units.leftText: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
units.rightText: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar, the shouts of captains and the cry of war.

units.leftText: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
units.rightText: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?

units.leftText: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
units.rightText: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?

units.leftText: On the cliff he dwells and makes his home, on the point of the cliff and the stronghold.
units.rightText: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.

units.leftText: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
units.rightText: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.

units.leftText: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
units.rightText: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”

units.leftText: Moreover the LORD answered Job,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Job:

units.leftText: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”
units.rightText: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered the LORD,
units.rightText: Then Job answered the LORD:

units.leftText: “Behold, I am of small account. What will I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
units.rightText: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.

units.leftText: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
units.rightText: I have spoken once, but I have no answer — twice, but I have nothing to add.” The LORD Challenges Job Again

units.leftText: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind:
units.rightText: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

units.leftText: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
units.rightText: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.

units.leftText: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
units.rightText: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?

units.leftText: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
units.rightText: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?

units.leftText: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
units.rightText: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.

units.leftText: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
units.rightText: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.

units.leftText: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
units.rightText: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.

units.leftText: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
units.rightText: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.

units.leftText: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
units.rightText: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.

units.leftText: “See now behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
units.rightText: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.

units.leftText: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
units.rightText: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.

units.leftText: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
units.rightText: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.

units.leftText: His bones are like tubes of bronze. His limbs are like bars of iron.
units.rightText: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.

units.leftText: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
units.rightText: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.

units.leftText: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
units.rightText: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.

units.leftText: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
units.rightText: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
rightNotes: 40:21 Or bramble bushes; also in verse 22

units.leftText: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
units.rightText: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.

units.leftText: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
units.rightText: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.

units.leftText: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
units.rightText: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?[’’]

units.leftText: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
units.rightText: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
leftNotes: 41:1 Leviathan is a name for a crocodile or similar creature.

units.leftText: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
units.rightText: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?

units.leftText: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
units.rightText: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?

units.leftText: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
units.rightText: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?

units.leftText: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
units.rightText: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?

units.leftText: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
units.rightText: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?

units.leftText: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
units.rightText: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?

units.leftText: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
units.rightText: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!

units.leftText: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?
units.rightText: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?

units.leftText: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
units.rightText: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?

units.leftText: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
units.rightText: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.

units.leftText: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
units.rightText: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.

units.leftText: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who will come within his jaws?
units.rightText: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
rightNotes: 41:13 Or Who can come within his double mail?

units.leftText: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
units.rightText: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?

units.leftText: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
units.rightText: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.

units.leftText: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
units.rightText: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.

units.leftText: They are joined to one another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.
units.rightText: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.

units.leftText: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
units.rightText: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.

units.leftText: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
units.rightText: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!

units.leftText: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
units.rightText: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.

units.leftText: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
units.rightText: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.

units.leftText: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
units.rightText: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.

units.leftText: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.
units.rightText: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.

units.leftText: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
units.rightText: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!

units.leftText: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
units.rightText: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.

units.leftText: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
units.rightText: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.

units.leftText: He counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.
units.rightText: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.

units.leftText: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.
units.rightText: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.

units.leftText: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
units.rightText: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.

units.leftText: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
units.rightText: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.

units.leftText: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
units.rightText: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.

units.leftText: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.
units.rightText: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!

units.leftText: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.
units.rightText: Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!

units.leftText: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”
units.rightText: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered the LORD:
units.rightText: Then Job replied to the LORD:

units.leftText: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
units.rightText: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.

units.leftText: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I didn’t understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.
units.rightText: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.

units.leftText: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’
units.rightText: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’

units.leftText: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
units.rightText: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.

units.leftText: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”
units.rightText: Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.” The LORD Rebukes Job’s Friends

units.leftText: It was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.
units.rightText: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.

units.leftText: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”
units.rightText: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”

units.leftText: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD commanded them, and the LORD accepted Job.
units.rightText: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer. The LORD Blesses Job

units.leftText: The LORD restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends. The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
units.rightText: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.

units.leftText: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that the LORD had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.
units.rightText: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
leftNotes: 42:11 literally, kesitah, a unit of money, probably silver
rightNotes: 42:11 Hebrew a kesitah; the value or weight of the kesitah is no longer known.

units.leftText: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
units.rightText: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

units.leftText: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
units.rightText: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.

units.leftText: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
units.rightText: He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.

units.leftText: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
units.rightText: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.

units.leftText: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
units.rightText: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.

units.leftText: So Job died, being old and full of days.
units.rightText: And so Job died, old and full of years.
